records.prompt:
Snow accumulates on Janet's driveway from midnight to 9 a.m. at rate
\[
f(t)=7te^{\cos t}
\]
cubic feet per hour, where \(t\) is hours after midnight. Janet removes snow at rate
\[
g(t)=\begin{cases}
0,&0\le t<6,\\
125,&6\le t<7,\\
108,&7\le t\le9.
\end{cases}
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: How many cubic feet of snow have accumulated by 6 a.m.?

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the rate of change of the volume of snow on the driveway at 8 a.m.
parts.answer:
The net rate is accumulation minus removal:
\[
f(8)-g(8)=7(8)e^{\cos8}-108
\approx\boxed{-59.583\ \text{ft}^3/\text{hour}}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Let \(h(t)\) be the total snow removed by time \(t\). Express \(h\) as a piecewise function on \([0,9]\).

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: How many cubic feet of snow are on the driveway at 9 a.m.?
parts.answer:
Total accumulation is
\[
\int_0^9f(t)dt\approx367.335.
\]
The amount removed is \(h(9)=125+216=341\). Hence
\[
\boxed{367.335-341\approx26.335\ \text{ft}^3}.
\]

records.prompt:
A zoo contest receives entries in a box between noon and 8 p.m. The differentiable function \(E(t)\), in hundreds of entries, has values
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccccc}
t&0&2&5&7&8\\\hline
E(t)&0&4&13&21&23
\end{array}
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Approximate the rate at which entries were deposited at \(t=6\).
parts.answer:
Using the closest points bracketing \(6\),
\[
\boxed{E'(6)\approx\frac{E(7)-E(5)}{7-5}
=4\ \text{hundred entries/hour}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the trapezoidal rule to approximate \(\frac18\int_0^8E(t)dt\), and interpret.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: From 8 p.m. to midnight, entries are processed at rate \(P(t)=t^3-30t^2+298t-976\) hundreds per hour. How many entries remain unprocessed at midnight?

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: According to the model, at what time were entries processed most quickly? Justify.
parts.answer:
\[
P'(t)=3t^2-60t+298,
\]
with critical points
\[
t=10\pm\frac{\sqrt6}{3}.
\]
Comparing \(P\) at these points and at \(t=8,12\) gives the largest value \(P(12)=8\). Thus
\[
\boxed{t=12\text{, midnight}}.
\]

records.prompt: There are initially \(700\) people in line for a ride. While a line exists, people board at \(800\) people per hour. The arrival rate \(r(t)\) is the supplied piecewise-linear graph through \((0,1000)\), \((2,1200)\), \((4,400)\), \((6,400)\), and \((8,0)\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: How many people arrive between \(t=0\) and \(t=3\)?
parts.answer:
From \(0\) to \(2\), the trapezoid area is
\[
2\frac{1000+1200}{2}=2200.
\]
At \(t=3\), \(r(3)=800\), so the area from \(2\) to \(3\) is \(1000\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{3200\ \text{people}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Is the number in line increasing or decreasing between \(t=2\) and \(t=3\)?
parts.answer:
On \((2,3)\), the arrival rate satisfies \(r(t)>800\), so arrivals exceed boarding. Thus
\[
\boxed{\text{the line is increasing}}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: At what time is the line longest, and how many people are in line then?
parts.answer:
The line grows while \(r(t)>800\) and begins shrinking when \(r(t)<800\); the transition occurs at \(t=3\). The number then is
\[
700+\int_0^3r(t)dt-800(3)
=700+3200-2400
=\boxed{1500}.
\]
Thus the line is longest at
\[
\boxed{t=3\ \text{hours}}.
\]

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Write, but do not solve, an equation whose solution gives the earliest time at which there is no longer a line.
parts.answer:
The number in line at time \(t\) is
\[
700+\int_0^t(r(x)-800)dx.
\]
Thus the earliest empty-line time solves
\[
\boxed{700+\int_0^t(r(x)-800)dx=0}.
\]
